title: A punctured-root section descends to a pointed affine etale neighbourhood
statement: Let i:U→L and π:P→U be scheme morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with π finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let R be a commutative ring, φ:Spec R→L and f∈R any element. Let β:U×_L Spec R≅D(f) commute with projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix any n≥0, a geometric point barY:Spec Ω→Spec R over y, and H=the canonical strict henselization ring [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let b:R→H induce its structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put A_H=H[T]/(T^n-b(f)), q_H:Spec A_H→Spec H and V_H=D(b(f)). Suppose there is s_H:V_H→P satisfying s_H;π;i=V_H→Spec A_H→Spec H→Spec R→L. Then there are a commutative ring S, a:R→S and z∈Spec S, with Spec(a) etale and Spec(a)(z)=y. Put g=a(f), A_S=S[T]/(T^n-g), q_S:Spec A_S→Spec S and V_S=D(g). There is s_S:V_S→P satisfying s_S;π;i=V_S→Spec A_S→Spec S→Spec R→L. No torsor, ramification, regularity or nonzerodivisor assumption, and no positivity or invertibility assumption on n, is required; the existence of the section over H is an explicit hypothesis.

proof.text: Use beta and hbeta to show pullback.snd i phi is locally of finite presentation: it is an isomorphism followed by an open immersion. The iterated-pullback isomorphism identifies E=P times_L Spec R with P times_U (U times_L Spec R); its structural map p is locally of finite presentation, being the base change of the etale map pi followed by the preceding locally finitely presented map. Lift the given punctured-root section to E by the pullback universal property. Finiteness of pi is not used.

Compare strictHenselizationRing with the adopted strictHenselization by the unique isomorphism of colimits of the same representative affine diagram. Its coprojection equations and the structural-map leg equations prove compatibility over Spec R. Compose b with this isomorphism and apply the adopted punctured root limit presentation. The root base-change theorem along this ring isomorphism identifies the adopted punctured chart with the original one: the second pullback projection is an isomorphism because the spectrum of the ring comparison is an isomorphism. The pullback condition and first-projection equation identify the chart structure maps. Compose its inverse with the limit comparison to obtain the original-model limit isomorphism and its leg equations.

Using the transported limit presentation, all diagram terms are affine, hence qcqs, and their transitions are affine. Transport the lifted section through the inverse of the limit isomorphism e. The equations for the structure maps, canceled through e, show this is a morphism over Spec R. Apply the Mathlib finite-presentation map limit factorization theorem to p and this morphism.

The resulting index supplies S, a, z and the isomorphism d from its punctured root chart. Compose d with the descended map to E and the projection E -> P. The pullback condition and the descended map structure equation, followed by the equation d;t_j=k_S, prove the required equality over L. Retain the supplied etaleness and point equation.
